findings.title: The partial unique index does not constrain NULL stripe_subscription_id, and conversion_duplicate_exists? returns early on a blank id -- unlimited conversion rows per NULL are possible, but the webhook can never produce one
findings.file: db/schema.rb:1199 (idx_subscription_events_conversion_stripe_sub_id, unique, where event_type = ANY (ARRAY[2,8])); app/interactors/create_subscription_event.rb:58 (return unless context.stripe_subscription_id.present?)
findings.evidence: Live, script /tmp/qa5_agent9_adversarial_a.rb. T2b: two SubscriptionEvent.create! converted_to_paid rows with stripe_subscription_id nil BOTH persisted (no RecordNotUnique) and each fired its own PosthogTrackJob (2 enqueues) -- Postgres treats NULLs as distinct in a unique index. REACHABILITY PROVEN NEGATIVE for the webhook, live: Stripe::Subscription.retrieve(nil) raises LOCALLY, before any HTTP, with Stripe::InvalidRequestError "Could not determine which URL to request: Stripe::Subscription instance has invalid ID: nil" (stripe-9.4.0 api_resource.rb:69-78 resource_url, reached from retrieve -> new -> refresh). Delivering an invoice.paid whose object.subscription is nil WITHOUT stubbing Stripe::Subscription.retrieve: the handler's rescue Stripe::StripeError tier absorbed it, ZERO rows written, zero fan-out, no raise escaped. The main-plan branch (and therefore the writer) is entered only after that retrieve succeeds, so object.subscription is always a real subscription id at the writer.
findings.reachability: Not reachable from either sanctioned webhook insertion. Only reachable through the console/backfill row-creation path SPEC §11.3 already accepts. Every script in this round ran with allow_any_instance_of(Stripe::StripeClient).to receive(:execute_request).and_raise(...) as a loud guard; it never fired, so zero real Stripe HTTP was attempted anywhere in the round.

findings.title: conversion_duplicate_exists? queries SubscriptionEvent globally, not scoped to the organization -- a conversion row owned by organization A blocks a conversion row for organization B on the same stripe_subscription_id
findings.evidence: Live with two REAL seeded orgs, script /tmp/qa5_agent9_adversarial_c.rb T7/T7b. Organization A id 37146 (owner 41123), Organization B id 37147 (owner 41124), shared id sub_a9_c_shared. A's converted_to_paid succeeded (row 3438, organization_id 37146, amount 1000); B's identical call for the same subscription id FAILED with 'Conversion SubscriptionEvent already exists for stripe_subscription_id sub_a9_c_shared'; exactly one row exists and it belongs to A; exactly one PosthogTrackJob fired and its distinct_id was 41123 (A's owner), so B got no PostHog event. Reproduced through the REAL invoice.paid webhook for B's customer cus_a9_c_orgb: no second row, no raise, no PostHog -- and B's pre-existing branch behavior still ran (stripe_current_period_end_at written to 2026-08-27 15:08:39).
findings.reachability: Not reachable as a defect. Stripe subscription ids are globally unique within a Stripe account, so one subscription maps to one customer and Organization.find_by(stripe_customer_id:) resolves to one organization. When it does happen, the outcome (exactly one conversion row per subscription) is precisely SPEC §3's binding invariant, which the spec itself documents as 'strictly tighter than D7's organization + stripe_subscription_id wording'. Recorded so the global-scope behavior is on the record as observed rather than assumed.

findings.title: Repeat trial_started: a second nil -> 'trialing' flip past the 5-minute dedupe writes a second trial_started row with full fan-out, even on the SAME stripe_subscription_id
findings.evidence: Live, scripts /tmp/qa5_agent9_adversarial_b.rb T5a/T5b and /tmp/qa5_agent9_adversarial_c.rb (T5a redo). Two nil->trialing flips on org 37146 with stripe_subscription_id held at sub_a9_c_trial1, the first row backdated 30 minutes to defeat the dedupe: 2 trial_started rows for the SAME subscription id, and each flip independently enqueued its own PosthogTrackJob + Discord::NotifyFreeTrialStartedJob (first flip [Notification::FreeTrialStartedJob, PosthogTrackJob, Discord::NotifyFreeTrialStartedJob], second flip identical). T5b: a re-trial on a NEW subscription id (sub_a9_b_trial2 / sub_a9_c_clean) also writes its own row -- that shape is spec-consistent per SPEC §5.1 (no uniqueness index on event_type 7).
findings.reachability: NOT reachable in production. Reaching a second flip requires stripe_subscription_status to return to nil. Traced every assignment: the only production code that sets it to nil is Organization#stripe_delete_customer (app/models/organization.rb:503), which raises StandardError when Variables::ServerEnv == 'production' (app/models/organization.rb:494); sync_with_stripe assigns stripe_subscription_status only inside `if current_subscription.present?` (app/models/organization.rb:568-571) and never nils it; Cypress::OrganizationsController:14 writes 'canceled', not nil. Both flips above required update_column to force the status back to nil.

findings.title: A delayed invoice.paid for a superseded subscription writes a row keyed on the event's subscription id but stamped with the organization's CURRENT plan, which may not be the plan that subscription was on
findings.evidence: Live, script /tmp/qa5_agent9_adversarial_b.rb T10. Org 37145 with stripe_subscription_id column = sub_a9_b_current and plan = plan_ats_tier_starter received an invoice.paid for subscription sub_a9_b_old (amount_paid 1500, trial_end 60 days ago). Row 3434 written: stripe_subscription_id 'sub_a9_b_old', to_plan 'plan_ats_tier_starter' (the CURRENT plan, not necessarily the old subscription's), event_type trial_converted_to_paid, amount 1500. No raise, existing branch behavior intact.
findings.reachability: Reachable but narrow -- requires a retried or delayed invoice.paid for a subscription the org has already replaced, and only produces a wrong to_plan when the replacement changed plans. This is exactly what SPEC §5.2 specifies (to_plan: organization.plan, stripe_subscription_id: object.subscription), so it is spec-compliant, not a spec-implementation mismatch. Recorded as an accuracy property of the ledger, not a defect.

verified: INTERACTOR RecordNotUnique RESCUE PATH DRIVEN (nobody had): with a real converted_to_paid row present for sub_a9_t1 and conversion_duplicate_exists? stubbed to return false (stub effectiveness asserted live), CreateSubscriptionEvent.call did NOT raise, returned context.failure? == true with message 'Conversion SubscriptionEvent already exists for stripe_subscription_id sub_a9_t1', wrote no row, and fired no fan-out. The DB partial unique index was the only thing that stopped the duplicate.

The DB connection survives the rescued RecordNotUnique -- SubscriptionEvent.count executed immediately afterwards returned 1 with no 'current transaction is aborted' error, so ActiveRecord rolled the failed save's transaction back cleanly.

Same race driven through a REAL invoice.paid delivery: the webhook completed without raising, the ledger still held exactly one row for sub_a9_t1, no fan-out fired from the blocked insert, and BOTH pre-existing effects ran -- stripe_current_period_end_at advanced to 1808838252 and (re-asserted in /tmp/qa5_agent9_adversarial_b.rb R3 with a falsifiable signal) organization_ai_credit_balance.last_reset_at moved 2026-05-27 -> 2026-07-27.
